messages.subject: Issue with composite variable
parts:
Dear  lavaan users,

apologies for the total beginner's question. I am trying to create a composite variable and I have done it successfully, but I am bit confused about how to fix the scale. I am attaching some data with a few lines of codes, to show what puzzles me. Please bear in mind that this is just an example and my composite will have many more variables! What I do not understand is the parameter estimate for my composite. In its non-composite version it is negative and then it becomes positive on one occasion.

# read data set
dat<-read.csv("newdf.csv")

# no composite
no.compo<-'F~T'
standardizedSolution(sem(no.compo,data=dat))

#1) fix scale of composite using parameter estimate from model without composite

compo1<-'lat<~-0.061*T
          F~lat'
standardizedSolution(sem(compo1,data=dat))


#2) fix scale of composite fixing path of baseline indicator to 1

compo2<-'lat<~1*T
          F~lat'
standardizedSolution(sem(compo2,data=dat))

#3) fix scale of composite using parameter estimate from model without composite (using absolute value of parameter estimate)
compo3<-'lat<~0.061*T
          F~lat'
standardizedSolution(sem(compo3,data=dat))

Okay, if I have understood correctly 1 and 3 should be equivalent to 2. There are just two different ways of fixing the scale. Is this correct? But, why, when I fix the scale using 3 I get results equal to 2, something that makes more sense in the light of the relationship between the two variables of interest? Should I always fix the scale using the unstandardized parameter estimate without the minus sign, if this is negative?

Apologies for these simple questions, but I am a bit lost! Is there any comprehensive book dealing with these issues? I have searched for one, but no book seems to deal with this in an exhaustive manner.


thanks in advance!

Simone

messages.subject: Re: Issue with composite variable
parts:
On 08/12/2014 10:34 PM, Simone Ruzza wrote:
> I do not understand is the parameter estimate for my composite.

It looks to me that fixing the scale by using 1* is the most natural
approach here.

To 'better' see how composites are treated within lavaan, use the

inspect(fit, "est")

function, and observe how the parameters map to the model matrices.

Yves.
